title: Microsoft Purview: retention based on last accessed date for SharePoint and OneDrive files
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned Office-file deletion capability and Microsoft's revised rollout windows. Its general retention controls are documented, and it keeps the separate archiving preview's access-history behaviour distinct from the still-undocumented Purview option.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes retention for SharePoint and OneDrive items based on their last access by a user.
claims.quote: This creates the ability to apply Retention to each SharePoint or OneDrive item based on when it was last accessed by a user.

claims.claim: MC999442 announces retention policies or retention labels for OneDrive and SharePoint files nobody in the organisation has accessed for a period.
claims.quote: Enable admins to apply retention policy or retention label in OneDrive and SharePoint for files that have not been accessed by anyone in the organization after a period of time.

claims.quote: When the content was last modified. Supported only for files in the SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 Groups locations.

claims.claim: The date content was labelled is a documented retention-period starting point.
claims.quote: When the content was labeled. Available with retention labels, for documents in SharePoint and OneDrive, and for email items.

claims.claim: An event is a documented retention-period starting point.
claims.quote: When an event occurs. Available with retention labels that are configured for event-based retention, such as when employees leave the organization or contracts expire.

claims.claim: The announced last-accessed trigger adds another retention starting point to the four currently described by Learn.
claims.quote: After the rollout, admins can use the retention control When items were last accessed when configuring labels and policies.

claims.claim: Last access date updates for the archive preview can take up to 30 days.

claims.quote: Storage consumption is charged at a per-GB monthly rate. This meter is charged only when archived storage plus active storage in SharePoint exceeds the included or licensed allocated SharePoint storage capacity limit of the tenant.

claims.claim: A newly created file archive policy is Inactive.
claims.quote: The policy is created in an Inactive state and must be activated using Set-SPOFileArchivePolicy with -State Active before it takes effect.

claims.claim: Set-SPOFileArchivePolicy -PolicyId <guid> -State Active activates an archive policy.
claims.quote: Set-SPOFileArchivePolicy -PolicyId "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890" -State "Active" ... Activates the specified file archive policy.

claims.claim: A SelectedSites archive policy requires at least one included site before activation.
claims.quote: To activate a SelectedSites policy, at least one site must have been added as an inclusion using Add-SPOSiteToFileArchivePolicy without -Exclude. Excluded sites don't satisfy this requirement.

claims.where: Governance controls: archive prose; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An Active archive policy with IsWhatIfMode set to true evaluates and reports without archiving.
claims.quote: | Active | `$true` | Evaluate and report without archiving files. |

claims.claim: Whether the new retention control starts enforcing without configuration is not stated, so its control-level default is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview When items were last accessed retention policy configure default. Read roadmap, MC999442, retention and create-retention-policies. MC999442 states availability by default, but does not state automatic enforcement or changes to existing retention configurations.

claims.claim: For the archive preview, choosing an inactivity period after July 2025 gives a more complete observation period but does not exclude older recorded access dates.
claims.quote: For critical content, choose an inactivity period that falls entirely after July 2025. This provides a more complete observation period; it doesn't exclude files with older LADs.
